MAJOR: `diff_reviews(committed=True)` treats an empty `ls-tree` as "unreadable or empty" and raises; a branch with no committed reviews (a legitimate state) is indistinguishable from a git failure and hard-exits 2, making the gate fail-always rather than fail-closed.

Attestation fails open when evidence has no/empty `sha`: `latest = max(...)["sha"]` can be `""`, and `churn_attested` skips the citation check via `if latest_sha and ...`, so an over-budget item is allowed by an attestation that cites nothing.

precheck groups `review-churn` under "backlog" while its sibling Gate 2.5 gate `architect-review` is "quality"; if group determines which precheck runs where, the churn budget may not run on the path that enforces Gate 2.5/completion.

`redact_reason` has no generic secret patterns (`sk-…`, private-key-less high-entropy tokens, `--token <val>` form); the redacted-but-partial reason is persisted into `engineering/reviews` evidence that is committed to git — secret residue can ship.

Re-review archive (`-prev-<ms>.json`) makes one physical review count as two evidence rows for the same sha, inflating churn counts and triggering the warn budget on a legitimate, reasoned re-review (enshrined by `test_archived_rereview_counts_as_a_run` but contradicting "one diff review per freeze" counting integrity).
MINOR: `--json` combined with `--report` writes a non-JSON `REPORT` line to stdout after the JSON document; and scan errors in `--json` mode emit no structured output at all, breaking machine consumers.

`review_guard` returns the redacted reason but `main` discards it and re-redacts the raw input; if the cited sha falls past the 500-char cap the stored `rereview_reason` omits the very sha it was validated against.

`--reason` without `--rereview` is only rejected in diff mode (`reason_flag_error` inside `if a.mode == "diff"`); design-mode `--rereview --reason` silently stores `rereview_reason` with no validation.
The committed git path (`ls-tree`/`show` in `diff_reviews` and `_item_committed`) has zero test coverage — fail-closed tests only exercise the working-tree corrupt-file path.
Threshold defaults `2`/`4` are duplicated as code fallbacks in `review_budget()` and hardcoded again in `docs/REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE.md` prose, risking drift from `config/architect-review.json`.
`redact_reason` is invoked twice per run (guard + main) with different inputs/outputs discarded, an avoidable divergence point for future edits.
NIT: Unrelated reformat of `blocking_findings`/`skip_globs` in `architect-review.json` adds config churn orthogonal to BI-PF-1480.
`churn_verdict` computes `allowed = not (over and not attested)` alongside `fail = over and not attested`; one expression should derive from the other.
Docs line renders an ASCII `-` where an arrow/em-dash is intended, and the pre-existing binding-order line uses `?` placeholders.
SUMMARY: Solid single-owner design: thresholds, epoch, counting and attestation are correctly centralized in `architect_review.py` and consumed by both entry points, with boundary/HIL/fail-closed tests largely present.

Top risks: fail-always (not fail-closed) on an empty committed review tree, fail-open attestation when `sha` is empty, possible churn-count inflation from `-prev-` archives, and incomplete secret redaction before evidence is committed.
Secondary: precheck group placement may silently skip the gate, machine output purity under `--json --report`, and the untested committed-git read path.
